records.source: Ἐρωτῶμεν δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ὑπὲρ τῆς παρουσίας τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἡμῶν ἐπισυναγωγῆς ἐπ’ αὐτόν, εἰς τὸ μὴ ταχέως σαλευθῆναι ὑμᾶς ἀπὸ τοῦ νοὸς μηδὲ θροεῖσθαι μήτε διὰ πνεύματος μήτε διὰ λόγου μήτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ὡς δι’ ἡμῶν, ὡς ὅτι ἐνέστηκεν ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου.
records.gloss: We ask now you, brothers, concerning the coming of the Lord of us Jesus Christ and of our gathering together to him, \v 2 for the not quickly to be shaken you from the mind nor to be alarmed, neither through spirit nor through word nor through letter as through us, as that has come the day of the Lord.
pieces: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we have a request about the coming of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and our gathering to meet {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

Do not let yourselves be quickly shaken out of your senses or thrown into alarm by a prophetic word, a spoken message or a letter that claims to come from us, saying that the day of the Lord is already here.

L.1: Now we ask you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and our being gathered together to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
L.2: not to be quickly shaken from [your] mind or alarmed, either by a spirit or by a word or by a letter as if from us, to the effect that the day of the Lord has come.

R.1: {{gender:Brothers and sisters|Brothers}}, we want to talk to you about when our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} comes back and gathers us to {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.
R.2: Some people may say that the day of the Lord has already come. Do not be quick to get upset or worried by this, even if someone says it came from the Spirit, or from something we said, or from a letter we wrote.

decisions.choice: our gathering together to him
decisions.reason: ἐπισυναγωγῆς is the gathering of believers to the Lord at his coming, which 1 Thessalonians 4:17 describes; Jesus used the related verb of the angels gathering his chosen ones (Mark 13:27).

decisions.choice: a spirit: a prophetic utterance claiming to come from the Spirit
decisions.reason: πνεύματος here is a message given in the church as from the Spirit (1 Thessalonians 5:19-21, where such words are to be tested).

decisions.choice: as if from us: someone was claiming Paul's authority
alternatives: a genuine letter of Paul's misunderstood
decisions.reason: ὡς δι ἡμῶν goes at least with "letter" and perhaps with all three. Someone may have passed on a letter falsely claiming to be Paul's, which would explain why he signs this one so carefully (3:17), or misread his first letter.

decisions.choice: has come: is already here
decisions.reason: ἐνίστημι in the perfect means "has arrived, is present" (Romans 8:38, "things present"). The false claim was not that the day was near, which Paul himself taught, but that it had already come.

decisions.choice: shaken and alarmed
decisions.reason: σαλευθῆναι is to be shaken like a ship in a storm; θροεῖσθαι is to be startled, thrown into alarm (Mark 13:7).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: a prophetic word, a spoken message or a letter (B); from the Spirit, ... from something we said, or from a letter we wrote (R)
alternatives: a spirit, a word, a letter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "a spirit" means here (m2).

records.heading: The man of lawlessness

records.source: μή τις ὑμᾶς ἐξαπατήσῃ κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον· ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἔλθῃ ἡ ἀποστασία πρῶτον καὶ ἀποκαλυφθῇ ὁ ἄνθρωπος τῆς ἀνομίας, ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ὁ ἀντικείμενος καὶ ὑπεραιρόμενος ἐπὶ πάντα λεγόμενον θεὸν ἢ σέβασμα, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καθίσαι ἀποδεικνύντα ἑαυτὸν ὅτι ἔστιν θεός.
records.gloss: Not anyone you should deceive in any way; because unless comes the rebellion first and is revealed the man of the lawlessness, the son of the destruction, \v 4 the [one] opposing and exalting himself over every so-called god or object of worship, so that he in the temple of the God sits, showing himself that he is God.
pieces: No one must lead you astray, whatever they say. Before that day comes, the great rebellion must first take place, and the man of lawlessness must be unveiled, the one doomed to destruction.
He will set himself against every so-called god and everything people worship, and lift himself above them all, until he takes his seat in God's temple and presents himself as God.

L.3: Let no one deceive you in any way, because [that day will not come] unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
L.4: who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or object of worship, so that he takes his seat in the temple of God, displaying himself as being God.

R.3: Do not let anyone fool you in any way. That day will not come until there is a great rebellion against God, and until the man who rebels against all of God's laws appears. He is headed for destruction.
R.4: He will fight against everything that people call a god or worship. He will say he is greater than all of them. He will even sit in God's temple and say that he is God.

decisions.choice: [that day will not come] unless: the main clause is left unsaid
decisions.reason: The Greek gives only the condition; the obvious conclusion, "that day will not come", is left for the reader to supply from verse 2.

decisions.choice: the rebellion: a final, known revolt against God
alternatives: a departure of believers from the earth
decisions.reason: ἀποστασία means rebellion or defection, in the Greek Old Testament revolt against God (Joshua 22:22). The article marks it as the rebellion Paul had taught them about (verse 5). Some have read it as the departure of the church from the world, but the word has the sense of revolt elsewhere.

decisions.choice: the man of lawlessness, the son of destruction: one who embodies defiance of God and is doomed
decisions.reason: "Man of" and "son of" are Hebrew ways of saying what a person is marked by: he is lawlessness in person, and he is destined for destruction (John 17:12 uses "son of destruction" of Judas). The letter does not name him, and the many identifications readers have proposed go beyond what it says.

decisions.choice: exalting himself above every god, sitting in God's temple: the arrogant rulers of Daniel and the prophets
decisions.reason: The words echo the king of Daniel 11:36, who "will exalt himself above every god", and the ruler of Tyre who said "I am a god, I sit in the seat of God" (Ezekiel 28:2). Jewish memory held Antiochus IV, who set up a pagan altar in the temple in 167 BC, and the emperor Gaius, who in AD 40 ordered his statue placed there.

decisions.choice: the temple of God
alternatives: a picture of God's dwelling, or of the church (1 Corinthians 3:16)
decisions.reason: ναὸν is the word for the sanctuary. The temple in Jerusalem was standing when Paul wrote, and he may mean it; or the language may picture a claim to God's own place, without a particular building in view.

decisions.choice: [that day will not come]
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves the main clause to be understood (m1).

decisions.choice: the one doomed to destruction (B); He is headed for destruction (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain the idiom (m3).

decisions.choice: a great rebellion against God; the man who rebels against all of God's laws
alternatives: the rebellion; the man of lawlessness
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rebellion and lawlessness are (m2, m3).

records.source: οὐ μνημονεύετε ὅτι ἔτι ὢν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ταῦτα ἔλεγον ὑμῖν;
records.gloss: Not do you remember that still being with you these things I was telling you?
pieces: Surely you remember: I kept telling you this while I was still with you.

L.5: Do you not remember that while I was still with you I was telling you these things?

R.5: Do you remember? When I was still with you, I told you these things.

decisions.choice: I kept telling you: Paul himself, more than once
decisions.reason: The imperfect ἔλεγον and the singular "I" show that Paul had taught them about this in person and often. That is why he can be brief here, and why some of what he says is hard for later readers: they knew what he meant (verse 6).

decisions.choice: Surely you remember
decisions.reason: The question expects "yes"; Balanced says so.

records.source: καὶ νῦν τὸ κατέχον οἴδατε, εἰς τὸ ἀποκαλυφθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν τῷ ἑαυτοῦ καιρῷ·
records.gloss: And now the restraining [thing] you know, so that to be revealed him in the of himself time;
pieces: And you know what is holding him back now, so that he will be revealed only when his time comes.

L.6: And you know what is restraining [him] now, so that he will be revealed in his own time.

R.6: You know what is stopping him from appearing now. He will appear only at the time that has been set for him.

decisions.choice: what is restraining: a power holding back the lawless one, which the Thessalonians knew and we do not
alternatives: the Roman empire and its emperor
decisions.reason: κατέχον is neuter here ("what restrains"), and in verse 7 masculine ("the one who restrains"), so it may be a force with a person behind it. Paul says the Thessalonians know what it is; he does not say. All the proposals listed are guesses. κατέχω can also mean "hold sway", which would change the picture, though "restrain" fits "until he is taken out of the way" (verse 7).

decisions.choice: in his own time: the time set for him
decisions.reason: The lawless one cannot appear before his appointed time: even his coming is under God's control.

decisions.choice: what is stopping him from appearing
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sense without naming the restrainer (m1).

records.source: τὸ γὰρ μυστήριον ἤδη ἐνεργεῖται τῆς ἀνομίας· μόνον ὁ κατέχων ἄρτι ἕως ἐκ μέσου γένηται.
records.gloss: The for mystery already is at work of the lawlessness; only the [one] restraining now until out of [the] midst he is gone.
pieces: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work, but only until the one who now holds it back is taken out of the way.

L.7: For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work; only [there is] the one who restrains now, until he is taken out of the way.

R.7: The mystery of lawlessness is already at work in the world, in ways people cannot see. But someone is holding it back now, until that one is taken out of the way.

decisions.choice: the mystery of lawlessness: rebellion against God at work in hidden ways
decisions.reason: Elsewhere μυστήριον is God's plan, once hidden and now made known (Colossians 1:26). Here, as a dark counterpart, it is lawlessness already at work beneath the surface, before it shows itself openly in the lawless one.

decisions.choice: until he is taken out of the way: removed
decisions.reason: ἐκ μέσου ("out of the midst") means removed, out of the way. Who removes him, and how, is not said.

decisions.choice: the one who restrains: masculine here (see verse 6)
decisions.reason: See the note on verse 6.

decisions.choice: in ways people cannot see
decisions.reason: Readable says why it is called a mystery (m1); the key term "mystery" stays at every level.

records.source: καὶ τότε ἀποκαλυφθήσεται ὁ ἄνομος, ὃν ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς ἀνελεῖ τῷ πνεύματι τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ καὶ καταργήσει τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, οὗ ἐστιν ἡ παρουσία κατ’ ἐνέργειαν τοῦ Σατανᾶ ἐν πάσῃ δυνάμει καὶ σημείοις καὶ τέρασιν ψεύδους καὶ ἐν πάσῃ ἀπάτῃ ἀδικίας τοῖς ἀπολλυμένοις, ἀνθ’ ὧν τὴν ἀγάπην τῆς ἀληθείας οὐκ ἐδέξαντο εἰς τὸ σωθῆναι αὐτούς·
records.gloss: And then will be revealed the lawless [one], whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of the mouth of him and will bring to nothing by the appearing of the coming of him, \v 9 whose is the coming according to [the] working of the Satan with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood \v 10 and with all deceit of unrighteousness for those perishing, because the love of the truth not they received so as to be saved them.
pieces: Then the lawless one will be unveiled, and the Lord Jesus will destroy him with the breath of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth and bring him to nothing by the brightness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.
The lawless one comes by Satan's working, with all kinds of power, with false signs and wonders,
and with every evil trick to deceive those who are on the way to ruin. They are lost because they would not welcome the love of the truth, which would have saved them.

L.8: And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will kill with the breath of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mouth and bring to nothing by the appearance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.
L.9: [The lawless one's] coming is by the working of Satan, with every [kind of] power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
L.10: and with every deception of wickedness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so as to be saved.

R.8: Then the lawless man will appear. But the Lord Jesus will destroy him just by breathing on him, and will bring him to an end by the brightness of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} coming.
R.9: Satan will give the lawless man power to come and to do all kinds of powerful things. He will do signs and wonders, but they will all be lies.
R.10: He will use every kind of evil trick to fool people who are on the way to destruction. They will be destroyed because they did not want to love the truth, which would have saved them.

decisions.choice: with the breath of his mouth: Isaiah 11:4
decisions.reason: The coming king of Isaiah 11:4 "will kill the wicked with the breath of his lips". A word from Jesus is enough.

decisions.choice: bring to nothing by the appearance of his coming
decisions.reason: καταργέω is to make powerless, abolish. ἐπιφανείᾳ is a shining appearance, used of a god showing himself or a ruler's arrival: his coming in splendor ends the lawless one.

decisions.choice: whose coming: the lawless one's, a counterfeit of Christ's
decisions.reason: οὗ refers to the lawless one. Paul uses for his arrival the same word, παρουσία, as for Christ's coming: a mocking imitation.

decisions.choice: power, signs and wonders of falsehood: all of them serving the lie
decisions.reason: ψεύδους ("of falsehood") most likely describes all three: real or not, they serve deception (Mark 13:22).

decisions.choice: those who are perishing: on the way to ruin
decisions.reason: The present ἀπολλυμένοις describes people heading for destruction (1 Corinthians 1:18).

decisions.choice: they did not receive the love of the truth: they refused the gospel
decisions.reason: The truth is the gospel (verses 12-13). They are not merely misled: they would not welcome what would have saved them.

decisions.choice: [The lawless one's]
decisions.reason: Literal names the one referred to (m3).

decisions.choice: just by breathing on him
alternatives: with the breath of his mouth
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

records.source: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο πέμπει αὐτοῖς ὁ θεὸς ἐνέργειαν πλάνης εἰς τὸ πιστεῦσαι αὐτοὺς τῷ ψεύδει, ἵνα κριθῶσιν πάντες οἱ μὴ πιστεύσαντες τῇ ἀληθείᾳ ἀλλὰ εὐδοκήσαντες τῇ ἀδικίᾳ.
records.gloss: And because of this sends to them the God [a] working of delusion so that to believe them the lie, \v 12 so that may be judged all those not having believed the truth but having taken pleasure in the unrighteousness.
pieces: That is why God sends them a deluding power, so that they put their trust in the lie,
and judgment comes on all who refused to believe the truth and chose to take pleasure in what is wrong.

L.11: And for this reason God sends them a working of delusion so that they believe the lie,
L.12: so that all may be judged who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness.

R.11: So God sends them a power that fools them, and they believe what is false.
R.12: Then God will judge everyone who did not believe the truth but enjoyed doing wrong.

decisions.choice: God sends them delusion: his judgment gives them over to what they chose
decisions.reason: Those who refused the truth (verse 10) are handed over to the lie they preferred, as in Romans 1:24-28, where God "gave them over", and 1 Kings 22:22-23. God's sending is a judgment on their choice, not its cause.

decisions.choice: the lie: the great lie set against the truth
decisions.reason: The article points to a particular lie, most likely the lawless one's claim to be God (verse 4), the opposite of "the truth".

decisions.choice: judged: condemned
decisions.reason: κρίνω here means judged and found guilty.

records.source: Ἡμεῖς δὲ ὀφείλομεν εὐχαριστεῖν τῷ θεῷ πάντοτε περὶ ὑμῶν, ἀδελφοὶ ἠγαπημένοι ὑπὸ κυρίου, ὅτι εἵλατο ὑμᾶς ὁ θεὸς ἀπαρχὴν εἰς σωτηρίαν ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος καὶ πίστει ἀληθείας, εἰς ὃ ἐκάλεσεν ὑμᾶς διὰ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ἡμῶν, εἰς περιποίησιν δόξης τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
records.gloss: We but ought to give thanks to the God always concerning you, brothers having been loved by [the] Lord, because chose you the God [as] firstfruits for salvation in sanctification of [the] Spirit and faith in [the] truth, \v 14 to which he called you through the gospel of us, for [the] obtaining of [the] glory of the Lord of us Jesus Christ.
pieces: But we must always thank God for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} whom the Lord loves, because God chose you, as the first of a harvest, to be saved, through the Spirit who makes you holy and through your faith in the truth.
To this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you when we brought you the gospel, so that you would come to possess the glory of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

L.13: But we ought always to give thanks to God for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} loved by [the] Lord, because God chose you as firstfruits for salvation, through sanctification by [the] Spirit and faith in [the] truth,
L.14: to which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called you through our gospel, for obtaining the glory of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.

R.13: But we must always thank God for you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. The Lord loves you. God chose you to be among the first to be saved. He made you holy by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, and you put your faith in the truth.
R.14: God called you to this when we told you the good news. He did this so that you could share in the glory of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "as firstfruits"
decisions.reason: The two readings differ by a single letter in the Greek capitals of the oldest manuscripts, and both have good support. "Firstfruits", the first of a harvest offered to God, fits Paul's usage (Romans 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:15): the Thessalonians are among the first believers in Macedonia. "From the beginning" would stress that God chose them before time. Reviewers should check the evidence.

decisions.choice: through the Spirit's work of making holy and through faith in the truth
decisions.reason: God's side and theirs: the Spirit sets them apart for God, and they believe the truth (contrast verse 12).

decisions.choice: loved by the Lord: Jesus
decisions.reason: "The Lord" is Jesus, set beside "God chose you". The words recall Deuteronomy 33:12, "the beloved of the LORD".

decisions.choice: obtaining the glory: coming to possess it
decisions.reason: περιποίησιν is the word of 1 Thessalonians 5:9, "obtaining salvation". They will share the glory of Christ (1:10, 1:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: as the first of a harvest (B); among the first (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable explain "firstfruits" (m1).

records.heading: Chosen to be saved

records.source: ἄρα οὖν, ἀδελφοί, στήκετε, καὶ κρατεῖτε τὰς παραδόσεις ἃς ἐδιδάχθητε εἴτε διὰ λόγου εἴτε δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ἡμῶν.
records.gloss: So then, brothers, stand firm, and hold fast the traditions which you were taught whether through word or through letter of us.
pieces: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, keep standing firm, and keep a firm grip on the traditions you were taught by us, whether we spoke them in person or wrote them in our letter.

L.15: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, stand firm and hold fast the traditions that you were taught, whether by word [of mouth] or by our letter.

R.15: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, stand strong. Hold on to the teachings we gave you, both what we said to you in person and what we wrote to you in our letter.

decisions.choice: traditions: the teaching handed on by the apostles
decisions.reason: παραδόσεις is teaching passed on (1 Corinthians 11:2; 15:3). Unlike the "human tradition" of Colossians 2:8, this tradition comes from the Lord through his messengers.

decisions.choice: our letter: the letter they had received
decisions.reason: Most likely 1 Thessalonians. Paul's genuine teaching, spoken or written, is the answer to the false claims of verse 2.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: The letter is to the whole church, women and men; "brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

records.source: Αὐτὸς δὲ ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς καὶ θεὸς ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν, ὁ ἀγαπήσας ἡμᾶς καὶ δοὺς παράκλησιν αἰωνίαν καὶ ἐλπίδα ἀγαθὴν ἐν χάριτι, παρακαλέσαι ὑμῶν τὰς καρδίας καὶ στηρίξαι ἐν παντὶ ἔργῳ καὶ λόγῳ ἀγαθῷ.
records.gloss: Himself now the Lord of us Jesus Christ and God the Father of us, the [one] having loved us and having given eternal comfort and hope good in grace, \v 17 may comfort of you the hearts and strengthen [them] in every work and word good.
pieces: Our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and God our Father loved us and gave us eternal comfort and a good hope by grace.
May they comfort your hearts and steady them in every good deed and word.

L.16: Now may our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and God our Father, who loved us and gave [us] eternal comfort and good hope by grace,
L.17: comfort your hearts and strengthen [them] in every good work and word.

R.16: Our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} and God our Father love us. Because of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} grace, God has given us eternal comfort and a good hope.
R.17: We pray that they will encourage you and make you strong, so that you always do and say what is good.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus Christ and God the Father act as one
decisions.reason: Jesus is named first here, and the participles and verbs that follow are singular though both are their subject, as in 1 Thessalonians 3:11: what one does, the other does.

decisions.choice: eternal comfort: comfort that lasts into the age to come
decisions.reason: αἰωνίαν marks the comfort as belonging to the age to come: it does not fail when trouble comes.

decisions.choice: by grace: goes with "gave"
decisions.reason: The comfort and hope are a gift of God's free favor.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable divide the prayer into two sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek is one sentence; English reads more easily with the statement first and the prayer after.
